title: Nancay burst centers show no clear excess order similarity in 34 selected sessions of FRB 20220912A
abstract: We test whether consecutive detected burst groups have similar observed center frequencies in the public Nancay table for FRB 20220912A. In 34 selected sessions, 566 adjacent gaps of 5 to 1800 seconds give a mean frequency difference of 103.62 MHz. Random order within each session gives 105.80 MHz. The gap reduction is 2.06%, with a nominal session-bootstrap 95% interval of -3.64% to 7.75% and a one-sided shuffle probability of 0.254. Time cuts, close-burst grouping, signal strength, band-edge cuts, and a linear time control retain the null result. This separate telescope test agrees in direction of inference with an earlier CHIME null result. The frequency definitions differ. The supplementary times also differ from the paper examples by more than rounding alone. No precise physical memory limit or subsecond test is supported. Code, the exact source table, hashes, timing audit, controls, random draws and a figure are included.

display.caption: Measured frequency gaps and conditional random orders. All nominal session-bootstrap ranges include zero gap reduction.
